questions_and_answers.question_text: What kind of word is gè-?
What can gè- be prefixed to?
What happens when a gè- phrase is followed by dōu?
Which word is xǔduō a synonym of?
What do gèdì, gèrén, and gèzhǒng mean?

answers.answer_text: It is a polite form of address for a group of people, e.g., an audience.

questions_and_answers.question_text: Write the Chinese for "The teachers here are very concerned about the students."
Write the Chinese for "They use all kinds of modern machines."

articles.text:
6. A: Bù jǐn shi Rìběn, xiànzài      Not only Japan, all countries are now
      gèguó dōu hěn guānxīn          interested in the economic construction
      Zhōngguó yánhǎide jīngjì       of China's coast.
      jiànshè.
   B: Shì. Yǐjing yǒu xǔduō guójiā  Yes, there are already many countries
      xiǎng hé Zhōngguó yìqǐ zài     which are thinking of establishing new
      nèi yídài chénglì xīnde        companies with China in that area.
      gōngsī.

Notes on No. 6

gèguó: "various countries." GÈ-, "each and every," "various," is a SPECIFIER like zhèi-, "this," or nèi-, "that." You can prefix it to COUNTERS and to some NOUNS.

Wǒmen zài quánguó gèdì cānguān   We visited and toured all over the
yóulǎnle yíge yuè.               country for one month.
                                 (Gèdì is "each place," "various places.")
Xiànzài gèrén zuò gèrénde,       For now, everyone can do what they want.
sìdiǎn zài kāi huì.              We will have the meeting at four.
                                 (Gèrén is "everybody.")
Gèwèi rúguǒ yǒu shénme wèntí,    If you all have any questions, please
qǐng xiànzài tíchulai.           bring them up now. (Gèwèi is a polite
                                 form of address for a group of people.)
Tāmen yòng gèzhǒng xiàndàihuàde  They use all kinds of modern machines.
jīqì.                            (Gèzhǒng is "various kinds.")

When a GÈ- phrase is FOLLOWED by DŌU, "all," it takes on the meaning "EVERY," "ALL." Thus gèguó in 6A is translated as "all countries."

guānxīn: "to be concerned about," "to care about," "to be interested in" the WELFARE of something.

Zhèrde lǎoshī hěn guānxīn        The teachers here are very concerned
xuésheng.                        about the students.

xǔduō: "many," "a great deal (of)," "lots (of)." This is a SYNONYM of hěn duō, and used in the same ways.

chénglì: "to establish," "to found," "to set up"

Měiguó Diànhuà Diànbào Gōngsī    In what year was AT&T established?
shi něinián chénglìde?
